case: Identifies the shock, fiscal envelope or model assumption used for the simulation.
The scenario legend defines every observed code. Unspecified settings remain equal to the main configuration.
policy: Identifies the benchmark, unsupported shock or household support instrument.
baseline is the unshocked benchmark; shock is the no-policy equilibrium under the specified configuration. Policy codes are defined in the legend.
fgt0_pct: 100 times the person-weighted share with real equivalent disposable income below the fixed real poverty line.
Full-payment and zero-payment states of fractional boundary households are weighted separately. A lower value indicates a lower poverty headcount.
fgt1_pct: 100 × person-weighted mean[max(1 − y/z, 0)], where y is real equivalent disposable income and z is the fixed real poverty line.
The denominator is the full represented population, including non-poor people. A lower value indicates a smaller aggregate normalised income shortfall.
fgt2_pct: Places greater weight on deeper income shortfalls. Uses the same poverty line as FGT0 and FGT1; a lower value indicates lower poverty severity.
bottom40_ev_pct: 100 × sum of household-weighted money-metric welfare changes in the lowest two benchmark income groups / their total household-weighted initial consumption budgets.

The money-metric change is the policy real consumption budget minus its benchmark value. Group membership is fixed at the benchmark. A positive value is a gain; this is an expenditure-normalised aggregate rather than an average of household percentage changes.
all_ev_pct: 100 × sum of household-weighted money-metric welfare changes / total household-weighted benchmark consumption budgets.
Uses household expansion weights and household-specific cost-of-living deflation. A positive value indicates a gain relative to the unshocked benchmark.
bottom40_loser_pct: Share of bottom-40 persons losing consumption
100 times the person-weighted share in the lowest two benchmark income groups whose real consumption budget is below its benchmark level.
Receipt states are weighted separately. The numerical loss cutoff is the initial budget multiplied by (1 − 10⁻¹⁰), which removes roundoff at the benchmark.
micro_macro_demand_gap_pct: 100 × sum of absolute differences between micro-aggregated and CGE consumption expenditure across sector-by-quintile cells / total CGE household consumption expenditure.
Measures the demand discrepancy associated with heterogeneous household baskets versus representative group baskets. Values near zero indicate closer reconciliation.
max_group_budget_gap_trillion_tl: Largest absolute difference, across the five groups, between household-weighted micro consumption budgets and the corresponding CGE group budget.
An accounting diagnostic. The code checks that it is below 10⁻⁸ trillion TL. Very small scientific-notation values retain numerical roundoff.
negative_income_households: Number of distinct households with negative real equivalent disposable income in at least one receipt state with positive weight.
The zero-payment state is checked when mask < 1, and the full-payment state when mask > 0. This is a sample count, not an expanded national household total. S10 provides the boundary diagnostic.
gini: Person-weighted Gini coefficient of real equivalent disposable income, including the full-payment/zero-payment mixture for fractional recipients.
A lower value generally indicates lower inequality. Values are not multiplied by 100. Negative-income distributions require separate interpretation of the usual 0–1 range.
gdp_nominal_trillion_tl: Trillion TL in model price units
Model factor income + total tax revenue − household direct taxes − consumer price-support expenditure.
The wage is the numeraire. This is a current-price level; real GDP change is reported separately. One trillion TL equals 1,000 billion TL.
real_gdp_baseprice_pct: 100 × (final demand valued at benchmark prices / benchmark GDP − 1). Includes household consumption, public purchases, administration services, investment and net exports.
Relative to the unshocked benchmark. The code values final-demand quantities using the benchmark user-specific tax rates.
investment_baseprice_pct: 100 × (sum of sector investment quantities / benchmark total investment quantity − 1).
Relative to the unshocked benchmark. Quantities use unit benchmark-price normalisation. Treatment of negative net investment components depends on the scenario closure.
exchange_rate: The equilibrium exchange_rate variable: the normalised domestic-currency price of foreign currency.
For example, 1.01 indicates an increase of approximately 1%, rather than a 1.01% change. The index is measured relative to the fixed wage numeraire.
capital_rental: The wage is fixed at 1, so this measures the capital return relative to the wage numeraire. Its percentage change is 100 × (value − 1).
net_fiscal_cost_trillion_tl: Government saving in the same-shock no-policy equilibrium minus government saving in the policy equilibrium.
Includes tax and public-purchase-price feedbacks. Distinct from gross programme outlays. Recorded as zero for baseline and shock reference rows.
net_cost_gdp_pct: Net fiscal cost as a share of GDP
100 × net fiscal cost / unshocked benchmark GDP.
Main supported policies have value 0.5, meaning 0.5% of GDP. low_budget and high_budget use 0.25% and 1%, respectively.
net_cash_trillion_tl: Total new cash transferred directly to households, excluding administration expenditure (policy_cash).
Excludes households’ other income. Zero under price support. Under cash_saving_10pct, 10% of this payment is saved rather than consumed.
price_support_trillion_tl: Sum of discount rate × pre-support tax-inclusive price × household consumption quantity across supported sectors and household groups.
Calculated using equilibrium quantities. Zero under cash policies.
admin_cost_trillion_tl: Administrative rate / (1 − administrative rate) × net cash. Spent on public administration services, sector S54.
The main rate is 3% of gross cash-programme spending. zero_admin and high_admin change that rate. No separate price-support administration cost is specified in this component.
gross_program_cost_trillion_tl: Net household cash + administration expenditure + consumer price-support expenditure.
Can differ from final net fiscal cost because taxes and public-purchase prices adjust in equilibrium.
tax_revenue_trillion_tl: Equilibrium T: the total of production, product and direct-tax revenue components.
Includes relevant product taxes on public and administrative purchases. Negative net tax components retain their signs.
government_saving_trillion_tl: Tax revenue less the current cost of real public purchases, cash transfers, administration expenditure and consumer subsidies.
Its decline relative to the same-shock no-policy reference defines net fiscal cost. It contributes to investment financing under the savings-driven closure.
consumer_discount_pct: Applies only to household purchases of eligible goods. This is not the total CPI change. Zero under cash policies.
sector: Unique activity identifier in the 64-sector SAM and CGE model.
The sector legend links each identifier to its NACE code and activity name. Codes are consistent across inputs and outputs.
nace: National-accounts activity classification corresponding to the model sector.
L68A denotes imputed owner-occupied housing services; L68B denotes other real estate. These are model-specific subdivisions.
output_pct: 100 × (policy equilibrium output Z / benchmark output Z0 − 1).
In this CSV, the reference is the unshocked benchmark. The value combines shock and support effects; it is not the incremental support effect relative to the unsupported shock.
composite_price_pct: 100 × (domestic–import composite supply price pq − 1), with benchmark pq = 1.
A composite supply price, distinct from the final household purchaser price including consumption taxes and support discounts.
imports_volume_trillion_tl: Trillion TL equivalent at benchmark prices
Model import quantity M. Unit benchmark-price normalisation expresses quantities on a benchmark monetary-value-equivalent scale.
Not tonnes, physical units or the current import bill. Current value requires multiplication by the corresponding import price. Benchmark zero-import sectors retain zero flows.
exports_volume_trillion_tl: Trillion TL equivalent at benchmark prices
Model export quantity E, reported on a monetary-equivalent scale at unit benchmark prices.
Not physical units or current export revenue. Current value requires multiplication by the export price. Benchmark zero-export sectors retain zero flows.
exclusion: Share of eligible persons not receiving cash: 1 − recipient population within the target / target population, using person weights.
Eligibility is membership in the lowest two benchmark equivalent-income groups. 0.30 means 30%. S4/S5 use design coordinates; S6 computes the realised rate from recipient allocation.
leakage: Share of cash reaching non-eligible recipients. Under equal-per-person payments, equals non-eligible recipient population / total recipient population.
0.30 means 30%. The denominator is all recipients, not all non-eligible persons. In S6, fixed total coverage equal to target-population size implies leakage = exclusion.
seed: Identifies one of ten random recipient allocations at a given experimental level.
The actual random seed is 20261025 + seed in S4 and 20261025 + 100 + seed in S6. This column stores the draw index, not the complete random seed.
difference_vs_universal_pp: FGT1 of the specified targeted-cash allocation minus FGT1 under main-scenario universal cash.
Negative values favour targeted cash; positive values favour universal cash. Uses the common main shock and net fiscal budget. This is a percentage-point difference, not a percentage change.
mean_difference_pp: Arithmetic mean of the ten difference_vs_universal_pp values in the same exclusion–leakage cell.
A negative mean indicates a targeting advantage. The error-grid ranking surface is based on these cell means.
seed_sd_pp: Sample standard deviation of the ten policy differences within the cell; pandas std uses ddof = 1.
Describes variation across recipient draws. It is neither a standard error nor a 95% confidence interval.
min_seed_difference_pp: Minimum policy difference among the ten draws in the exclusion–leakage cell.
More negative values indicate a larger targeted-cash advantage. This is the lower endpoint of the draw range, not a confidence bound.
max_seed_difference_pp: Maximum policy difference among the ten draws in the exclusion–leakage cell.
Upper endpoint of the recipient-draw range, distinct from a conditional bootstrap confidence bound.
level: r2_* denotes the target R² of the out-of-fold PMT income score after adding noise. independent denotes a separately generated independent random score.
Nine finite levels: 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0, −0.5, −1, −2, −4 and −8. Ten recipient draws per level, plus ten independent-score draws, give 100 rows.
r2: 1 − person-weighted mean squared prediction error / person-weighted variance of log(1 + equivalent disposable income). Noise is scaled to attain the specified target exactly.
For finite levels, the code checks that achieved and target R² differ by less than 10⁻¹⁰. Blank for independent-score rows because R² is not reported there; blank does not mean zero.
coverage: Represented persons receiving cash / total represented population.
S6 holds coverage at the lowest-two-quintile population share, approximately 0.399903. Fractional boundary weights provide exact person-weighted coverage.
poverty_line_fraction: Multiplier applied to benchmark person-weighted median equivalent income to define the fixed real poverty line.
0.5, 0.6 and 0.7 mean 50%, 60% and 70% of the median. Within each measurement variant, the line remains fixed across policies.
homogeneous_within_quintile: False uses each household’s calibrated sector budget shares. True assigns the CGE group budget shares to every household in that quintile.
Changes household price indices and micro demand composition. Policy equilibria and recipient lists remain fixed in this measurement-sensitivity exercise.
category: S00–S02 are Agriculture, S03–S26 are Industry and S27–S63 are Services in the model code.
A reporting classification. Elasticities are read separately for each sector.
sigma: CES substitution elasticity between domestic and imported varieties within a sector.
Uses GTAP 11 ESUBD mappings and adaptations for mixed activities. sigma_source documents each mapping. The import branch is inactive in zero-import sectors.
psi: Constant elasticity of transformation governing allocation of sector output between domestic sales and exports.
Uses a positive ψ convention. Benchmark assumptions are 1.12 for agriculture, 0.601 for industry and 0.5 for services. The export branch is inactive in zero-export sectors.
omega: Capital–labour substitution elasticity in the value-added nest.
Assigned from Turkish industry estimates and GTAP factor-substitution proxies. Reported values in single-factor sectors do not activate two-factor substitution. omega_source gives the adaptations.
sigma_source: Author, year, table, source parameter, sector mapping, aggregation convention and DOI/URL for σ.
Copied verbatim from the selected-elasticity workbook’s Armington sheet, source-and-adaptation column. Original-language source quotations are retained.
psi_source: Source publication, broad activity assumption, positive transformation convention and DOI/URL for ψ.
Copied verbatim from the selected-elasticity workbook’s CET sheet, source-and-adaptation column. Original-language source quotations are retained.
omega_source: Turkish estimate or GTAP proxy, sector adaptation, single-factor convention and DOI/URL for ω.
Copied verbatim from the selected-elasticity workbook’s CES sheet, source-and-adaptation column. Original-language source quotations are retained.
negative_households: Households with negative real equivalent income
Count of households whose reconstructed real equivalent disposable income is below zero in the specified unsupported-shock reference.
Only flagged configurations are included. The current output contains one affected sample household, not an expanded national household count.
affected_population_pct: Population share affected by negative income
100 × person-weight sum for negative-income households / person-weight sum for all households.
A represented-person share, not a percentage of sample households.
minimum_real_equivalent_income_hbs_tl: Annual HBS-equivalent TL per equivalent adult
Smallest reconstructed real equivalent disposable income in the configuration, after reversing macro scaling and deflating by the household price index.
Uses the 2024 HBS income scale, not trillion TL. The negative value records the boundary case associated with the factor-income-indexed micro reconciliation residual.
poverty_line_hbs_tl: Annual HBS-equivalent TL per equivalent adult
60% of benchmark person-weighted median equivalent disposable income.
The S10 diagnostic holds this line fixed and changes only the negative-income treatment.
original_fgt1_pct: Poverty gap using original reconstructed incomes
100 × person-weighted mean[max(1 − y/z, 0)] using original reconstructed incomes, including the negative observation.
Reproduces FGT1 for the corresponding case / shock row in S1.
zero_floor_fgt1_pct: Poverty gap after a zero-income floor
Replaces y with max(y, 0), then recomputes FGT1 using the same weights and poverty line.
A separate sensitivity diagnostic. The accounting-consistent income values in the main analysis are retained.
zero_floor_difference_pp: Effect of the zero-income floor on FGT1
Negative values indicate a reduction in measured poverty depth after flooring negative income at zero. Scientific notation preserves very small differences.
note: Code-generated explanation of the negative-income boundary case.
The current note attributes it to the factor-indexed micro reconciliation residual and confirms nonnegative disposable incomes in supported policy cases.
group: Person-weighted equivalent-income quintile fixed at the benchmark.
Q1 is the lowest-income group; Q5 is the highest.
ev_pct: Money-metric real consumption change normalised by initial spending within the quintile.
Relative to the unshocked benchmark; household-weight aggregation.
cpi_base100: Person-weighted mean of household-specific calibrated expenditure-share price indices within the quintile, multiplied by 100.
Values above 100 indicate higher purchaser prices.
recipient_person_pct: Person-weighted cash receipt within the quintile.
Price support has no cash recipients.
cash_share_pct: Cash received by the quintile divided by total household cash payments, times 100.
loser_pct: Person-weighted share with real consumption below its benchmark level.
A negative money-metric consumption change identifies a loss.
mean_exclusion_pct: Mean exclusion across ten recipient seeds, multiplied by 100.
Eligible persons excluded from cash receipt.
mean_leakage_pct: Mean leakage across ten recipient seeds, multiplied by 100.
Share of recipient persons outside the eligible population.
mean_fgt1_pct: Mean FGT1 across ten recipient seeds.
FGT1 is the person-weighted mean normalised poverty shortfall over all persons.
lower95_pp: 2.5th percentile of the combined recipient-seed and household-weight distribution of the paired FGT1 difference.
Targeted allocation minus universal cash; conditional on the model calibration.
upper95_pp: 97.5th percentile of the combined recipient-seed and household-weight distribution of the paired FGT1 difference.
Targeted allocation minus universal cash; conditional on the model calibration.
recipient_seeds: Number of recipient draws entering the level mean and combined conditional distribution.
Ten draws at each score level.
predictor_type: The data preparation is fitted independently in each training fold.
predictors: Inputs used in the predictor block.
19 categorical and 9 numeric inputs across five blocks.
predictor_count: Number of raw inputs in this block before one-hot expansion.
Counts do not refer to the final number of regression columns.
preprocessing: Preparation fitted on the training-fold records and applied to validation records.
Five shuffled folds; ridge penalty 10; seed 20261025; person weights normalised within folds.
output_relative_to_shock_pct: Relative to the unsupported main shock, matching the sector table in the Word supplement and Figure S4. The separate output_pct column uses the unshocked benchmark.
